documents.abstract: Abstract Background Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) pose a significant occupational health challenge for dental professionals due to prolonged static postures and repetitive movements. While obesity is a known risk factor for MSDs, its specific association with upper extremity disability among dentists remains underexplored.To investigate the association between body mass index (BMI) and work-related upper extremity disability among dentists in Arak, Iran. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 276 dentists recruited from dental offices and clinics in Arak using convenience sampling. Data were collected using a demographic and occupational questionnaire, the Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ), and the Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand (DASH) questionnaire. BMI was categorized according to World Health Organization criteria. Binary logistic regression and chi-square (χ²) tests were employed to determine factors associated with upper extremity disability. Statistical significance was defined as a p-value < 0.05. Results The prevalence of overweight and obesity was 36.6% and 19.2%, respectively. The shoulder was the most frequently affected site (58.7%), followed by the wrist/hand (53.6%) and neck (47.8%). After adjusting for gender, age, and work experience, overweight (adjusted OR = 1.84, 95% CI: 1.02–3.32, p = 0.04) and obesity (adjusted OR = 2.98, 95% CI: 1.42–6.25, p = 0.004) were significantly associated with higher odds of upper extremity disability compared to normal-weight dentists. No significant associations were observed for gender, age, or work experience. Conclusion Elevated BMI is independently associated with upper extremity disability among dentists in a dose-response manner. These findings highlight the need for integrated weight management and ergonomic interventions in occupational health strategies for dental professionals to reduce MSD burden.

Large Language Models (LLMs) have proven highly effective in automating software engineering tasks, bridging natural language and code semantics to achieve notable results in code generation and summarization. However, their scale incurs substantial computational costs, making full fine-tuning impractical. Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) methods like QLoRA enable efficient specialization with lower resource demands. Recent studies show QLoRA-optimized Large Code Models (LCMs) perform strongly across diverse tasks, yet it remains unclear whether this effectiveness persists when a single model is QLoRA fine-tuned for multiple code-related tasks. The interaction between Multi-task fine-tuning and QLoRA optimization, and how transfer learning affects correctness and quality of generated artifacts, remains largely unexplored. We investigate Multi-task QLoRA fine-tuning — a representative parameter-efficient method from the LoRA family — across three representative tasks: code generation, translation, and summarization. We evaluate functional correctness through execution-based and similarity-based metrics, complemented by comprehensive code quality analysis–an aspect largely overlooked in prior work. Our findings show that Multi-task QLoRA effectively leverages transfer learning, achieving competitive or superior performance at the 1.5B, 3B, and 7B configurations relative to both Single-task QLoRA and Multi-task full fine-tuning. Larger models demonstrate more consistent balance between correctness and quality, whereas smaller models preserve functionality but exhibit a higher incidence of quality-related issues.

Electrical automation teaching must prepare students to commission interconnected equipment, diagnose faults and judge technical changes against operating requirements. These tasks bring the relationship between new quality productive forces and vocational education into the classroom: industrial change reshapes competence requirements, while skilled graduates and college technical services can support the adoption and improvement of production technologies. This paper develops a teaching reform proposal for the three-year higher vocational Electrical Automation Technology programme. It combines policy and document analysis, conceptual comparison and instructional design, using the national professional teaching standard and research on project-based learning, workplace learning and authentic assessment. The analysis identifies coordination problems involving curriculum sequencing, practical training, enterprise participation, assessment and resource provision. A proposed project, upgrading a conveying and sorting cell while examining its energy use, connects programmable logic controller programming, variable-frequency drives, human-machine interfaces and industrial networking. Students move from requirement analysis and simulation to supervised commissioning, fault diagnosis and evidence-based review. Assessment combines project documentation and operating records with individual explanation and transfer tasks. The proposed reciprocal mechanism depends on translating workplace requirements into assessable learning tasks and returning reviewed teaching outcomes to enterprise discussion, staff training or technical service. These routes require sustained teacher coordination and explicit responsibility for accepting changes. The paper presents a design for subsequent piloting; it reports no institutional intervention or measured learning gains. A future evaluation should examine competence transfer separately from any claim about enterprise productivity, because a functioning classroom prototype provides insufficient evidence of industrial impact.

Waste pickers are among the occupational groups potentially exposed to biological hazards, including the hepatitis B virus (HBV), due to contact with waste materials and sharp objects in their working environment. This study aimed to describe the results of Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg) screening among waste pickers at three waste disposal sites in Malang City. A quantitative descriptive approach was employed involving 15 male waste pickers from Candi Panggung, Tlogomas, and Merjosari waste disposal sites, selected through purposive sampling. HBsAg screening was performed using capillary blood specimens with the immunochromatographic rapid test (ICT) method. The collected data were analyzed descriptively using frequency distributions and percentages. The results showed that the largest proportion of respondents was aged 40–50 years (33%), and all respondents (100%) had worked as waste pickers for more than five years. HBsAg screening identified 12 respondents (80%) with non-reactive results and 3 respondents (20%) with reactive results. These findings indicate the presence of reactive HBsAg screening results among the participants; however, further laboratory examinations are required to confirm their hepatitis B infection status. Due to the limited sample size and descriptive research design, the findings cannot establish the source of infection or a causal relationship between occupational exposure and HBV transmission. This study highlights the importance of occupational health education, appropriate personal protective equipment, and access to follow-up healthcare services for waste pickers.

documents.abstract: Breast cancer control in Indonesia is a government priority under the National Cancer Control Strategy 2024–2034, yet early prevention education has not equally reached adolescents with autism spectrum disorder and multiple disabilities. Rumah Autis recognizes this risk but faces limited understanding and a lack of inclusive breast self-examination (SADARI) educational media. Existing media mostly rely on lengthy texts, abstract verbal explanations, or sensory-unfriendly demonstrations, whereas adolescents with special needs require repeatable and easy-to-imitate visual information. Therefore, a program was conducted to develop and train 50 participants—comprising parents, volunteers, and the Rumah Autis caregiver team—on using artificial intelligence (AI)-based demonstration videos and pictogram cards called SADARI Ceria (Breast Self-Examination: Smart, Friendly, and Inclusive). Evaluation results showed that 68% of participants knew about SADARI, 96% understood the function of demonstration videos, 92% understood the function of pictogram cards, 42% were able to use both media, and 44% were moderately able to assist adolescents with special needs in recognizing bodily changes and communicating complaints to parents, caregivers, or health workers

ABSTRACT Informatics education requires instructional designs that connect conceptual understanding with procedural application and contextual problem-solving. This study aimed to develop an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-integrated course based on Problem-Based Learning (PBL) to support these two competencies among junior high school students. The product was developed using the Moodle platform by combining digital learning materials, problem-based activities, and AI support in the form of explanations and learning-material summaries. The needs analysis involved 113 students, while the learning-outcome evaluation employed an experimental group and a control group, each consisting of 34 students, using pretests and posttests. The needs analysis revealed percentages of 23% for decomposition, 50% for pattern recognition, 35% for abstraction, and 44% for algorithms. In procedural application of computational thinking, the experimental group's mean score increased from 58.40 to 82.60, whereas the control group's mean score increased from 57.90 to 70.30. For contextual problem-solving, the experimental group's mean score increased from 56.80 to 83.10, while the control group's mean score rose from 57.20 to 71.40. Descriptively, the experimental group demonstrated greater improvement in both measured competencies. These findings indicate the potential of the developed AI-integrated PBL course to support Informatics learning; however, its statistical effectiveness must be confirmed through inferential testing. ABSTRAK Pembelajaran Informatika membutuhkan rancangan pembelajaran yang mampu menghubungkan pemahaman konsep dengan penerapan prosedur dan penyelesaian masalah kontekstual. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengembangkan course terintegrasi Artificial Intelligence (AI) berbasis Problem-Based Learning (PBL) untuk mendukung kedua kemampuan tersebut pada siswa SMP. Produk dikembangkan melalui platform Moodle dengan memadukan materi digital, aktivitas pemecahan masalah, serta dukungan AI berupa penjelasan dan rangkuman materi. Analisis kebutuhan melibatkan 113 siswa, sedangkan evaluasi hasil belajar menggunakan kelompok eksperimen dan kelompok kontrol, masing-masing terdiri atas 34 siswa, dengan pengukuran pretest dan posttest. Hasil analisis kebutuhan menunjukkan persentase kemampuan dekomposisi sebesar 23%, pengenalan pola 50%, abstraksi 35%, dan algoritma 44%. Pada kemampuan penerapan prosedur berpikir komputasional, rata-rata kelompok eksperimen meningkat dari 58,40 menjadi 82,60, sedangkan kelompok kontrol meningkat dari 57,90 menjadi 70,30. Pada kemampuan pemecahan masalah kontekstual, rata-rata kelompok eksperimen meningkat dari 56,80 menjadi 83,10, sementara kelompok kontrol meningkat dari 57,20 menjadi 71,40. Secara deskriptif, kelompok eksperimen menunjukkan peningkatan lebih besar pada kedua kemampuan yang diukur. Hasil ini mengindikasikan potensi course yang dikembangkan dalam mendukung pembelajaran Informatika, tetapi efektivitas statistiknya masih perlu dipastikan melalui pengujian inferensial.

Background The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into blended learning requires pre-service teachers to develop AI-related competencies and the ability to integrate technology into pedagogy. This study examines how perceived AI literacy and technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK) are associated with deep learning through perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use. Methods A cross-sectional survey was completed by 423 pre-service teachers enrolled in blended learning courses at a university in China. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), with covariance-based structural equation modeling and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) used as complementary robustness and configurational analyses. Results Perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use significantly mediated the relationships between the two competencies and deep learning. All six indirect pathways were significant in both the PLS-SEM and covariance-based SEM analyses. The fsQCA revealed an equifinal and asymmetric structure: multiple, partly substitutable conditions were sufficient for high deep learning, and no single condition was necessary for either high or low deep learning. Conclusions The findings integrate the technology acceptance model and expectancy-value theory to explain how pre-service teachers' competencies and perceptions relate to deep learning in AI-enhanced blended environments. Teacher education should support technical competence alongside positive perceptions of AI's utility, usability, and value. Because the measures were self-reported and collected cross-sectionally at one university, the findings are interpreted as associational and configurational rather than causal.

Introduction As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms veterinary medicine, understanding stakeholder perceptions is crucial for its effective and responsible integration. To support the development of targeted educational and policy initiatives, this study aimed to evaluate the knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding AI among Bachelor of Veterinary Medicine (BVM) students, PhD students, faculty, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between December 2023 and March 2024 among BVM students, PhD students, and faculty members at City University of Hong Kong, and practicing veterinarians in Hong Kong who are members of the Hong Kong Veterinary Association. The survey assessed participants’ familiarity with AI, prior training, perceived benefits, concerns, and willingness to adopt AI in education and clinical practice. Descriptive and comparative analyses were performed to examine differences across stakeholder groups. Results Of 79 complete responses, nearly half (46.8%) reported unfamiliarity with AI concepts. Only 17.7% had received formal AI training, although 78.5% expressed interest in future AI education. Most respondents agreed that AI could enhance veterinary teaching and practice (83.5%) and 81.0% indicated they would likely incorporate AI tools into their work. Key perceived benefits included support for case-based learning (83.5%), virtual animal models for teaching (77.2%), and improved diagnostic accuracy (74.7%). However, 41.8% felt inadequately prepared to use AI. Major concerns included veterinarian accountability for AI-related harms (79.7%), lack of system flexibility (75.9%), and potential clinical inaccuracies (70.9%). Descriptively, practicing veterinarians reported the lowest AI tool use (66.7% had never used AI tools), the lowest preparedness (66.7% felt unprepared), and lower agreement with AI’s clinical benefits, although attitude differences were not statistically significant. Conclusion These exploratory findings suggest gaps in self-reported AI knowledge and differing perceptions of AI across veterinary stakeholder groups in Hong Kong, with AI use already widespread at the time of the survey despite limited formal training. While enthusiasm for AI integration is high, concerns about preparedness, accuracy, and ethical responsibility remain. Larger, multi-institutional studies are needed to confirm these patterns and to inform targeted training programs and ethical frameworks for safe and effective AI adoption in veterinary medicine.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots are increasingly incorporated into orthopedic education, yet their ability to handle complex, clinically oriented questions remains unclear. This study evaluates the accuracy, response time, and citation reliability of contemporary AI chatbots when answering adult reconstruction questions from the AAOS ResStudy question bank. METHODS: Fifty-five multiple-choice adult reconstruction questions were extracted and categorized by anatomic region (hip vs. knee), concept (clinical presentation, prognosis, management), and AAOS-defined difficulty. Seven chatbots (ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, ChatGPT-4o, Gemini, Gemini Advanced, Claude, and Co-Pilot) were assessed. Accuracy, response time, and citation quality (existence and relevance) were recorded. Statistical analyses included chi-square testing, t-tests, Pearson correlation, one-way ANOVA, and Kruskal-Wallis testing (p<0.05). RESULTS: Overall chatbot accuracy was 67.5%. GPT-4o performed best (80%), outperforming AAOS members (75%), while Co-Pilot ranked second (70.9%). Accuracy varied by concept, with highest performance in Clinical Presentation (78.6%) and lowest in Prognosis (63.1%). Difficulty strongly influenced performance, with accuracy dropping from 84.7% on very easy questions to 45.4% on difficult ones. Average response time was 3.6 seconds, and no significant correlation existed between speed and accuracy. Among citation-producing chatbots, Co-Pilot achieved 100% citation existence and relevance. CONCLUSION: Modern AI chatbots demonstrate moderate overall accuracy on adult reconstruction questions, with GPT-4o exhibiting the strongest performance. While chatbots excel at descriptive orthopedic knowledge, they continue to struggle with applied reasoning tasks such as prognosis and management. These findings support their use as supplementary, rather than primary, learning tools. Improving citation reliability and reasoning capabilities may enhance future educational applications. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: IV, Cross-Sectional Comparative Analysis.

documents.abstract: To identify, characterize, and critically appraise comparative economic evaluations and budget impact analyses of precision medicine strategies used to guide the use of high-cost medications for rheumatic and autoimmune diseases. The review will examine strategies based on biomarkers, pharmacogenomics, therapeutic drug monitoring, clinical decision rules, predictive models, machine learning, or artificial intelligence when the resulting information changes a treatment decision. The synthesis will cover incremental costs, quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs), net monetary benefit, cost savings, budget impact, affordability, value of information, and major sources of uncertainty, with particular attention to the transferability of findings to payers, health technology assessment (HTA) bodies, and public health systems.
topics: Health Systems, Economic Evaluations, Quality of Life

documents.abstract: Fly ash generated from coal-fired thermal power plants represents one of the largest industrial solid wastes worldwide and poses significant environmental challenges due to its high alkalinity, poor nutrient status, and elevated concentrations of potentially toxic elements such as arsenic (As), cadmium (Cd), chromium (Cr), lead (Pb), nickel (Ni), and mercury (Hg). The uncontrolled disposal of fly ash threatens soil quality, groundwater resources, ecosystem stability, and human health, highlighting the urgent need for sustainable remediation strategies. Among the available technologies, phytoremediation using native plant species has emerged as an environmentally friendly and potentially lower-input because indigenous plants are naturally adapted to local climatic and edaphic conditions, enabling long-term establishment and ecological restoration with minimal external inputs. This review critically synthesizes current knowledge on the physicochemical characteristics of fly ash, heavy metal speciation and bioavailability, and the physiological, biochemical, molecular, and rhizosphere-mediated mechanisms governing heavy metal uptake, translocation, detoxification, and sequestration in native plant species. Unlike previous reviews that primarily provide descriptive accounts of phytoremediation, this review integrates plant functional traits, rhizosphere interactions, soil microbial dynamics, and ecosystem restoration processes into a comprehensive framework for selecting suitable native species for fly ash rehabilitation. The review further discusses recent advances in microbiome-assisted phytoremediation, biochar-assisted remediation, omics technologies, artificial intelligence-assisted species selection, remote sensing, and ecological risk assessment as emerging tools for improving remediation efficiency and long-term restoration monitoring. Existing knowledge gaps, including limited long-term field validation, biomass disposal challenges, insufficient economic assessment, and the need for standardized evaluation criteria, are critically examined. Finally, the review proposes future research priorities and emphasizes the integration of phytoremediation with sustainable land management and environmental policy to support resilient ecosystem restoration and the long-term rehabilitation of fly ash-contaminated landscapes.

Health systems serving children have increasingly invested in social care initiatives, yet these programs frequently demonstrate inconsistent effectiveness and face challenges in sustainability and scalability. Precision social medicine (PSM) offers a framework for addressing this gap by leveraging artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) models to match social care interventions to patients' clinical and social context. This article presents a practical, 3-step approach for operationalizing PSM within health systems serving children. These steps are to (1) codefine precision in social care with patients and frontline staff, (2) translate that definition into an AI/ML-informed strategy for identifying risk and assigning services, and (3) test the approach in workflows before it impacts care. We highlight integrating such a framework using pediatric asthma as a case example, tailored for the pediatric hospitalist managing the transition from hospital to home.

documents.abstract: This technical report presents the research and development of a hierarchical Bayesian prediction system for the AIMS Predictive AI Evaluation Competition (PAIEC 2026), associated with NeurIPS 2026. The research addresses the problem of predicting the probability that an AI system correctly answers questions from previously unseen benchmarks under limited feedback. The evaluation setting involves making initial predictions without labels and subsequently updating predictions as selectively revealed labels become available. Methodology and Technical Contributions • Developed a compact hierarchical Bayesian prediction model incorporating benchmark-level offsets with heavy-tailed priors, pair-level ability, item difficulty pooled across subjects, and item-group effects. • Implemented exact posterior integration and Bayesian pooling to support prediction under sparse feedback and previously unseen benchmark conditions. • Designed a systematic experimental framework incorporating baseline comparisons, leave-one-benchmark-out (LOBO) evaluation, calibration analysis, leakage forensics, signal decomposition, and adversarial red-team experiments. • Established preregistered experiments, explicit statistical decision rules, reproducibility checks, automated validation, and competition submission pipelines. • Implemented the final prediction system using Python and NumPy. Selected Experimental Results • Local leave-one-benchmark-out evaluation (one subject per benchmark, 10 paired seeds): achieved a Brier ALC of 0.2088, compared with 0.2451 for the official baseline. • Official formative evaluation: achieved a mean Brier ALC of 0.1839 across four runs (standard deviation: 0.024). Lower Brier ALC indicates better performance. The local LOBO evaluation and official formative evaluation represent distinct experimental settings and should not be interpreted as a final competition ranking. Reproducibility and Research Artifacts The accompanying repository provides model implementations, experimental scripts, evaluation utilities, automated tests, competition submission artifacts, a technical report, and instructions for reproducing the reported results. The underlying gated measurement dataset is not redistributed and requires separate access. Repository: https://github.com/Shashwat-srivastav/s2wish-paiec2026 Keywords: Bayesian Statistics, Hierarchical Bayesian Modeling, Artificial Intelligence Evaluation, Benchmark Generalization, Probabilistic Prediction, Machine Learning, Statistical Calibration, Experimental Design, Reproducible Research.

Abstract Accurate and reliable rainfall forecasts are crucial for Early Warning Systems (EWS). Artificial Intelligence approaches, which post-process global physical forecasts, enable low-cost ensemble generation, extending skill to medium-range lead times and offering scalable systems to inform EWS particularly under resource-constrained settings. However, assessing their practical value in representing user-relevant rainfall extremes and guiding decisions for EWS remains critical. We present a low-cost, uncertainty quantification method that calibrates ensemble forecasts to probabilities of exceedances for rainfall extremes. Applied to raw and post-processed rainfall forecasts over East Africa, sub-regional analysis shows the threshold-calibrated, post-processed forecasts better reflecting the observed chances of extremes at higher rainfall thresholds. Case-study results show encouraging added value from post-processed forecasts at longer lead times. Forecast skill decomposed across rainfall and probability thresholds highlights the ranges of rainfall and risk tolerances where most actionable improvement arises, whether using satellite or rain-gauge data as reference. This tailored evaluation helps guide forecast adoption for EWS.

Objective To determine the combined effectiveness of personal factors in predicting motion sickness sensitivity elicited by linear motion of a sled. Background Technologies that create challenging motion environments have spurred the development of mathematical models aimed at predicting motion sickness. Including personal factors may improve their predictive accuracy. History of motion sickness, age, gender, and visual dependence have been identified as potential predictors, although their individual predictive value is limited. Method We assessed motion sickness history, age, and gender through a questionnaire. To evaluate visual dependence, participants oriented a virtual rod parallel to the orientation of gravity while observing a tilted static frame or a disc rotating in roll. Sensitivity is expressed using a new measure that considers both the magnitude and accumulation of self-reported symptoms. Results Our results confirmed the predictive value of history and showed a small yet significant contribution of dynamic visual dependence, with greater dependence associated with higher sensitivity ( R 2 = 25%). Recent history reported over the past 10 years was demonstrated as a better predictor than lifetime history. Age, gender, and static visual dependence did not enhance the prediction. Conclusion Combining multiple predictors shows little advantage for improving a prediction of sensitivity beyond history alone. Future studies could confirm the predictive value of dynamic visual dependence and seek to optimize recent history, for example, by restricting time period and motion environment. Application Improved prediction models may support tailoring system parameters to user sensitivity in technologies such as automated driving, head mounted displays, and simulators.

RETROSPECTIVE REGISTRATION. This registers the protocol (version 1.0, fixed 25 October 2026) of a systematic review comparing comprehensive orthodontic treatment with premolar extraction against comprehensive treatment without extraction, for every reported effectiveness and adverse-effect outcome. The protocol was fixed before screening but was not registered before screening began; this registration was made on 2 November 2026, after searching, screening, data extraction and analysis had been completed. All differences between the protocol and the completed review are reported in the manuscript (Table of protocol deviations). Purpose: to provide one review covering all premolar-extraction patterns and all outcomes (occlusion, treatment duration, soft-tissue profile, incisor and molar position, skeletal and vertical change, arch dimensions, smile, stability, root resorption, periodontal, airway, temporomandibular, patient-reported and third-molar outcomes), with risk of bias (RoB 2, ROBINS-I), random-effects meta-analysis, prediction intervals and GRADE certainty ratings, and an explicit comparison with earlier systematic reviews. The review was run as an AI-agent workflow under the supervision of the human guarantor (Prof Ahmed Elkhadem, Faculty of Dentistry, Cairo University).

Preregistration of a study testing whether a session-level detector based on effect signatures in trial-level data can separate human sessions from LLM agents and state-reading bots in online Stroop, n-back and parity judgment tasks. The files include the power analysis (for the three-paradigm design, see its addendum of 29 October 2026) and the feasibility runs of check 1. All agent sessions in these files are synthetic. Specialized skill courses are a crucial component of talent cultivation in physical education programs. However, their long duration and high intensity often lead to declines in student engagement, thereby affecting skill acquisition. Flow experience, as a key psychological indicator of learning states, can effectively reflect students’ actual level of involvement. Focusing on professional choice motivation, this study examined its relationship with flow experience in specialized skill courses among undergraduate physical education majors and further tested the three-way interaction among professional choice motivation, physical self-efficacy, and physical activity volume. Using the Professional Choice Motivation Scale, Physical Self-Efficacy Scale, Physical Activity Rating Scale, and the absorption subscale of the Flow Short Scale, data were collected on two survey occasions 3 months apart. A total of 398 valid responses were obtained at T1, and 203 valid responses were obtained when the T1 participants were surveyed again at T2. Because individual responses could not be matched across the two occasions, the two datasets were analyzed separately. Pearson correlation analysis, multiple linear regression, three-way interaction analysis, and conditional effect tests were performed using R. The results showed that both intrinsic motivation ( β T1 = 0.72, β T2 = 0.64, p T1T2 < 0.001) and extrinsic motivation ( β T1 = 0.61, β T2 = 0.53, p T1T2 < 0.001) were significantly and positively associated with flow experience at both survey occasions. Furthermore, the three-way interaction among professional choice motivation, physical self-efficacy, and physical activity volume was significant at both T1 and T2 and showed the same negative direction ( p T1T2 < 0.05). Conditional effect tests showed that, except for the high physical activity volume/high physical self-efficacy condition at T2, intrinsic motivation and extrinsic motivation were significantly and positively associated with flow experience under all other conditions. These findings contribute to a more contextualized understanding of the relationship between professional choice motivation and flow experience and offer important theoretical implications for instructional practice in specialized skill courses.

Prompt engineering shapes large language model (LLM) output, but practicing clinicians have little guidance on which prompting style suits a given clinical task. A single publicly available, de-identified pediatric psychiatric case report was submitted to a base, unauthenticated ChatGPT-5.5 session under four prompt conditions: zero-shot, chain-of-thought, role/persona, and structured/constrained output. Each output was scored from 0 (feature absent) to 2 (complete) on four criteria: diagnostic accuracy, causative agent recognition, safety completeness, and calibration. Output was compared against the published clinical course. Total scores were zero-shot 7/8, chain-of-thought 6/8, role-persona 7/8, and structured 7/8. All four conditions ranked bipolar I disorder above substance-induced psychotic disorder, whereas the treating team's documented differential favored unspecified and substance-induced categories without a confirmed bipolar diagnosis. All four conditions recommended neuroimaging, electroencephalography, and lumbar puncture, exceeding the workup the treating team actually performed. Across four prompt styles, core diagnostic content was materially the same; the styles differed in the precision of probability quantification and in reasoning transparency, not in the underlying differential generated.

documents.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools have made their way into English Language Teaching (ELT) contexts, yet their pedagogical value remains contested. While many learners engage with GenAI primarily as a quick hack for producing answers, fewer use it as a resource for reflective language learning. This study explores prompt writing as a language learning task that supports both language development and metacognitive awareness. The study was conducted with a target group of pre-seminary, tertiary-level learners with mixed linguistic proficiency. Over the course of four instructional sessions, the study used a classroom-based action research design. Learners engaged in cycles of prompt drafting, GenAI-generated responses, peer discussion, and prompt refinement. Classroom observations, learner reflections, and group discussions were used to gather qualitative insights. The findings indicate measurable improvement in learners’ autonomy, as learners became aware of how lexical choices shape meaning, along with increased engagement, teamwork, and reflective thinking. The study argues that prompt writing, when treated as a language task rather than a technical skill, can function as a practical tool for fostering metacognition in ELT classrooms.

Abstract: Psychosocial working conditions have become an increasingly relevant concern in occupational health, particularly in social care contexts where employees are exposed to demanding emotional and physical environments. This study examines the main psychosocial factors affecting workers in a Portuguese private social solidarity institution and explores their implications for well-being and productivity. A descriptive quantitative case study was conducted, supported by a literature review and a questionnaire applied to different professional groups within the organisation. The findings suggest that, although overall levels of psychosocial risk are relatively low, there are meaningful differences across occupational categories. Frontline care workers appear to be the most exposed group, followed by kitchen staff and technical personnel. Across the sample, emotional and physical demands, work pace, task overload and limited recognition emerged as the most significant factors. These results indicate that even in seemingly stable organisational environments, certain roles remain particularly vulnerable to psychosocial strain. The study underscores the importance of adopting preventive and organisational measures to foster healthier, more supportive working conditions, as these are essential for both employee well-being and the quality of care provided. Keywords: psychosocial risks, mental health, charitable organisations, working conditions, well-being at work. ___________________ Condições Psicossociais de Trabalho numa Instituição Portuguesa de Apoio Social: Um Estudo de Caso Descritivo por Grupo Profissional Resumo: As condições de trabalho psicossociais têm-se tornado uma preocupação cada vez mais relevante na saúde ocupacional, particularmente em contextos de assistência social, onde os trabalhadores estão expostos a ambientes emocional e fisicamente exigentes. Este estudo analisa os principais fatores psicossociais que afetam os trabalhadores de uma instituição privada de solidariedade social portuguesa e explora as suas implicações para o bem-estar e a produtividade. Foi realizado um estudo de caso quantitativo descritivo, apoiado por uma revisão da literatura e por um questionário aplicado a diferentes grupos profissionais dentro da organização. Os resultados sugerem que, embora os níveis globais de risco psicossocial sejam relativamente baixos, existem diferenças significativas entre as categorias profissionais. Os profissionais de cuidados na linha da frente parecem ser o grupo mais exposto, seguidos pelo pessoal de cozinha e pelo pessoal técnico. Em toda a amostra, as exigências emocionais e físicas, o ritmo de trabalho, a sobrecarga de tarefas e o reconhecimento limitado emergiram como os fatores mais significativos. Estes resultados indicam que, mesmo em ambientes organizacionais aparentemente estáveis, certas funções permanecem particularmente vulneráveis à tensão psicossocial. O estudo sublinha a importância de adotar medidas preventivas e organizacionais destinadas a promover condições de trabalho mais saudáveis e solidárias, uma vez que estas são essenciais tanto para o bem-estar dos colaboradores como para a qualidade dos cuidados prestados. Palavras-chave: riscos psicossociais, saúde mental, instituições de solidariedade social, condições de trabalho, bem-estar laboral.

Given the growing adoption of AI-driven diagnostic and treatment tools across health systems, understanding community awareness is crucial for effective integration and health communication. Applying the survey design, data were collected from 384 adult residents selected from across six Local Government Areas of Anambra State, Nigeria, using multistage and proportionate sampling techniques. Findings revealed a moderately high level of awareness of AI utilisation, with respondents expressing the strongest familiarity with AI-powered tools such as automated diagnostics and virtual assistants. Social media emerged as the dominant source of AI information, followed by traditional media, while healthcare providers contributed minimally to public knowledge. Respondents also recognised significant benefits of AI, including improved diagnostic accuracy, enhanced service delivery, and overall healthcare quality. However, concerns were evident regarding potential medical errors, privacy concerns, and job displacement of healthcare workers. These findings align with national and international studies showing high exposure but limited depth of understanding among the public and health workers. Guided by the Diffusion of Innovations and Agenda-Setting theories, the study concludes that public awareness is largely media-driven and remains at an early diffusion stage, underscoring the need for deliberate institutional communication, ethical safeguards, and structured public sensitisation. The study recommends strengthening health communication strategies, promoting data protection frameworks, and enhancing healthcare worker involvement in public AI education.

documents.abstract: Background: Plecanatide, which is used to treat irritable bowel syndrome constipation (IBS-C), is highly susceptible to gastric enzymatic degradation, impairing critical therapeutic efficacy and bioavailability. This work designed an improved site-directing, colon-targeted mucoadhesive formulation to guarantee site-specific delivery and efficacy. Methods: Design-Expert software 13 was used in a systematic optimization system with different concentrations of Na-alginate, Carbopol 934, and Methocel K15M. Flowability and compressibility were evaluated by pre-compression analysis. To specifically target the distal colon, the in vitro dissolution kinetics and cellular activity against the HCT116 colorectal carcinoma cells were assessed. They were in vivo studies that measured mucosal recovery, submucosal pathology, and systemic oxidative stress biomarkers (MDA and SOD). In the accelerated stability testing, the standardized periods were tested under controlled laboratory conditions. Results: Methocel K15M proved to be the best polymer. The formulation exhibited 24 h sustained release, which fit best in the Hixson–Crowell (r = 0.980) and Higuchi (r = 0.956) models. Cellular activity against the HCT116 cells was high (IC50 = 79.31 ug/mL), being ten-fold better than the raw API. In vivo, the mucoadhesive system demonstrated almost total inflammatory resolution of all the layers of the colon. As opposed to regular tablets, it had a tremendous impact in reducing MDA (p = 0.014) and raising the activity of SOD (p = 0.002). Accelerated stability testing (40 °C/75% RH for 6 months) showed a slight decrease in drug content from 100.85% to 96.78%, which remained within the acceptable pharmacopeial limits (90–110%), confirming formulation stability. Conclusions: The mucoadhesive Plecanatide formulation is a “site-directing colon-targeted mucoadhesive formulation” that can effectively overcome the shortcomings of traditional therapy; i.e., it exhibits the potential for better compliance. This formulation mitigates inflammatory and oxidative stress, offering a stable, promising alternative for managing chronic IBS-C symptoms and enhancing patient health outcomes in contemporary clinical practice and pharmaceutical standards.

Abstract The discovery of novel odorant molecules is key for the fragrance and flavor industries, yet efficiently navigating the vast chemical space to identify structures with desirable olfactory properties remains a significant challenge. Generative artificial intelligence offers a promising approach for de novo molecular design but typically requires large sets of molecules to learn from. To address this problem, we present a framework combining a variational autoencoder (VAE) with a quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) model to generate novel odorants from limited training sets of odor molecules. The self-supervised learning capabilities of the VAE allow it to learn SMILES grammar from ChemBL database, while its training objective is augmented with a loss term derived from an external QSAR model to structure the latent representation according to odor probability. While the VAE demonstrated high internal consistency in learning the QSAR supervision signal, validation against an external, unseen ground truth dataset (Unique Good Scents) confirms the model generates syntactically valid structures (100% validity achieved via rejection sampling) and 94.8% unique structures. The latent space is effectively structured by odor likelihood, evidenced by a Frechet ChemNet Distance (FCD) of ≈ 6.96 between generated molecules and known odorants, compared to ≈ 21.6 for the ChemBL baseline. Structural analysis via Bemis-Murcko scaffolds reveals that 74.4% of candidates possess novel core frameworks distinct from the training data, indicating the model performs extensive chemical space exploration beyond simple derivatization of known odorants. Generated candidates display physicochemical properties consistent with ground-truth odorants (mean MW ∼158 Da, LogP ∼1.67) and comparable predicted ADMET profiles. Furthermore, quantum mechanical calculations (GFN2-xTB) verify thermodynamic stability with energy distributions matching known volatiles, and automated retrosynthesis demonstrates practical viability, yielding valid synthesis routes for 100% of candidates, averaging 2.89 steps from commercially available precursors. This integrated approach provides a novel and systematic methodology for applying generative AI to explore chemical space specifically for the discovery of new candidate odorant molecules.

documents.abstract: Dual mandate - the federal College of Education act 2023 signed by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu legally and officially empowered these institutions to award education degrees while the NCE programmes continues. The Nigerian curriculum for biology at the senior secondary school level is designed to help students develop a range of skills which include understanding biological concepts and principles, application of the knowledge to solve real-life situations, problem solving skills and ability to communicate biological ideas and concepts effectively. Problem based learning is a pedagogical approach that involves students learning through the experience of solving real world problems. It is a student centered approach that encourages critical and creative thinking, collaboration, active learning and application of skills to solve real world problems. Problem based learning can be effectively integrated with STEM subjects; science, technology, education and mathematics. Problem based learning is grounded in several theories like constructivist, social constructivism posits by Vygotsky 1978. Artificial Intelligence has the potential to make up for the shortcomings of traditional problem based learning by giving full account of students reports in the project, timely feedback and helps teachers to monitor students learning outcome. AI tools used in education/science include machine learning algorithms; natural language processing techniques which are used to create personalized learning; AI powered VR or AR are also used. AI driven PBL used include Khammigo or custom GPT, Google Docs, Padlet AI, Gradescope, Google sheets etc. The global AI in education market size was estimated at USD 5.88 billion in 2024 is projected to grow at Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 31.2% from 2025 to 2030. However, with PBL, the teachers have to provide students with necessary resources e.g. learning materials, tools and technological support as well as guidance. One of the opportunities of integrating AI in education include personalized learning, creating more interactive and immersive learning experiences, games and simulations that boost students confidence, motivation and persistence leading to improved academic achievement.

Automated pose-estimation pipelines usually report one RULA or REBA score per frame, without indicating whether that decision would survive small errors in the estimated joint angles. Both instruments convert continuous angles into ordinal categories through fixed thresholds and non-additive lookup tables, so the same angular error may leave one decision unchanged while reversing another. Earlier vision-based studies report aggregate agreement with reference systems or experts; none attaches a robustness statement to the individual decision. This study proposes a reproducible protocol that does so. It combines an observability audit, conditional lower and upper bounds for decisions whose inputs cannot all be seen, controlled angle-level perturbation at magnitudes anchored to published single-camera angle errors (σ = 2, 5, 8, and 12°), and a set of metrics in which baseline decision retention (BDR) measures whether the reported decision survives and the Ergonomic Decision Stability Index (EDSI) measures the probability of the most frequent category after perturbation. The protocol was instantiated on one batik worker (four photographs, four videos). At the level of the RULA action level, the four photographed postures retained their lower-bound decision in at least 93% of replications at σ = 5°, although two of them lay only 0.1° and 0.2° from a component threshold, where distance-based predictors anticipated retention of only 21–52%. The same posture that was stable under RULA retained its REBA risk level in only 49% of replications. Unobserved inputs left the final action level undetermined between its bounds for every posture. Across 534 video frames, component-level stability fell from 0.88 at 2° to 0.40 at 12°. The results demonstrate the method on one case; they do not support population inference or a validated triage rule.
